messages:
Marta: thinking about shrinking the KV/prefix-cache contract surface. can we agree on a minimal API that still lets us do safe demote/handoff without exposing too many internals? :thinking:
Sam: +1. what are you picturing as "minimal"? just claim/release + notify?
Marta: yes. ClaimPrefix / ReleasePrefix / ReadHint (optional). keep eviction policy implementation detail behind node-local runtime. avoid explicit 'transfer' RPCs if possible.
Pranav: concern: without an explicit transfer, how do we ensure liveness on slow networks? blind release could cause two nodes to think they own the same prefix.
Marta: right — idea is to make ClaimPrefix idempotent and lease-based. Claim returns (granted, epoch, lease_ttl). if claim conflicts, runtime retries with backoff.
Elaine: sounds ok but we need a deterministic fallback for long-held leases (ops scenarios). ops-bot: incident alerting hook when claim retries exceed threshold.
Sam: I'd prefer a tiny explicit "relinquish_with_token" flow to avoid split-brain during sudden partition. token only valid for X seconds, signed by owner. keeps main API small but gives an escape hatch.
Marta: that's reasonable — keep token flow opt-in for the runtime to call during graceful handoffs. not in the common fast-path.
Pranav: tradeoffs: token requires owners to persist token state and signing keys. increases complexity for private deploys.
Marta: true. suggest token logic live in an optional sidecar that Dedicated/Private enable. hosted can leave it out. single core contract: Claim/Release/Probe. sidecar adds Relinquish(token) and ForcedClaim(token).
Elaine: metrics we should add before rolling: claim_latency, claim_conflicts, forced_claims_count, token_issue_rate, token_failures. also a gauge for in-flight ownership transitions.
Sam: test plan: chaos test with 3 nodes, randomized partitions + clock skew. assert safety (no two owners) and forward progress (some node owns). also run perf microbench to ensure common path (Claim success) < 200us p95.
Marta: sample proto for the minimal surface:```
service PrefixOwnership {
  rpc ClaimPrefix(ClaimRequest) returns (ClaimResponse);
  rpc ReleasePrefix(ReleaseRequest) returns (ReleaseResponse);
  rpc ProbePrefix(ProbeRequest) returns (ProbeResponse); // optional hint-only
}
```
Pranav: +1 on probe being hint-only. keep it cheap. also suggest a best-effort prefix-epoch telemetry in the response so controller can surface why a claim failed.
Marta: rollout: phased. start with runtime support behind feature flag, internal canary in non-critical clusters, then wider canary with token sidecar disabled. collect metrics for 72h, then enable token sidecar experiments in Dedicated.
Elaine: ops checklist: migration script to reconcile stale leases, CLI to force-release with admin auth, and a runaway-prefix alarm.
Sam: one more: keep the API versioned and small. version v1 = minimal. v1.1 adds token endpoints. v2 only if we must expose more semantics.
Marta: great. I'll write up a short follow-up RFC with the proto, metrics, canary steps, and test harness. thanks all. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: note: created ticket INF-6234 to track metrics + canary plan (link: https://redwood.example/t/INF-6234)
